therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: HMG-CoA reductase inhibition (statin) combined with intestinal cholesterol absorption inhibition (ezetimibe)
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: LDL-C reduction via dual inhibition of cholesterol synthesis and absorption
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Patients with hypercholesterolemia, coronary heart disease, or atherosclerosis requiring lipid-lowering therapy
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Percent change from baseline in LDL-C after 6 weeks combination treatment (mean of weeks 4 and 6)

results.target_engagement_evidence: LDL-C reductions during monotherapy phase: R10: -46.49%, R20: -53.59%, S40: -40.86%, S80: -46.35%; further reductions upon addition of ezetimibe confirm dual-pathway engagement
biomarker_changes: hs-CRP change: R10+E10 +107.12%, R20+E10 -9.53%, S40+E10 +15.03%, S80+E10 +0.42% (wide CIs, no consistent signal)
safety_signals: Serious adverse events were infrequent across all arms
Liver disorder reported in 1 patient on simvastatin 80 mg monotherapy
Cardiac events (AMI, angina, cardiac failure) reported sporadically across arms
Anaemia reported in 1 patient on simvastatin 80 mg + ezetimibe

dose_info.dose: Rosuvastatin 10 mg or 20 mg; Ezetimibe 10 mg; Simvastatin 40 mg or 80 mg
dose_info.schedule: Once daily; 6 weeks monotherapy followed by 6 weeks combination therapy

context.indication: Hypercholesterolemia with coronary heart disease or atherosclerosis
context.comparator: Simvastatin 40 mg or 80 mg + Ezetimibe 10 mg
context.duration: 12 weeks (6 weeks monotherapy + 6 weeks combination therapy)
